description: We are the reincarnation of the Children of the Sun, heirs to ancestral wisdom and guardians of the sacred balance of Pachamama. Guided by the power of Inti, we have awakened with a mission: to bring to light the flames that are consuming the forests of Peru and the world threatening life and shattering the harmony of our ecosystems. For where fire destroys, our consciousness must awaken.
summary: To empower local and regional governments in Peru with accessible, high-fidelity data to anticipate and manage forest fires—a devastating crisis that has resulted in 35 lives lost and over 63,000 hectares of forest affected in 2024 alone, with more than 39,000 wildfires reported over the last 24 years (Ministerio del Ambiente [MINAM], 2024)—we developed FuegoTrazo. Despite this severe threat, existing disaster management platforms in Peru suffer from critical regional data sparsity, leaving 85% of surveyed regional and local governments without any early warning system in 2024. Furthermore, global satellite fire records (MODIS and VIIRS) exhibit instrumental incompatibilities that hinder consistent long-term analysis. FuegoTrazo resolves these discrepancies by harmonizing multi-sensor hotspot records into a unified, statistically comparable metric. Employing an empirical calibration model based on conditional maximum likelihood, we standardized over two decades of satellite observations across a high-resolution 10x10 km national grid. The platform delivers a consistent historical burning activity calendar and integrates an experimental machine learning forecast module to project emergent fire risks. Ultimately, FuegoTrazo bridges a structural communication gap by decentralizing advanced Earth observation data, directly connecting national prevention teams with regional authorities to enable localized anomaly detection and data-driven emergency response.
details:
Knowing FuegoTrazo

What does it do?

FuegoTrazo is an interactive web-based burning activity calendar that harmonizes historical satellite fire hotspot records from MODIS and VIIRS sensors into a web application, filtering and querying data accurately using official boundary polygons. By adjusting data to a common scale across Peru, it allows users to:

  • Analyze fire activity at a granular spatial level using a 10x10 km grid system in an interactive heatmap.
  • Monitor fire activity trends on a weekly basis.
  • Identify unusual burning conditions and critical periods.
  • Filter and query fire data accurately using official boundary polygons.
  • Generate a custom preventive plan.
  • Generate a fire activity prediction model.
  • Generate and download a custom territorial report in PDF format.
  • Learn about emergency contacts for fire activity in Peru.
  • View and analyze the data harmonization process.
  • Allows to read the webpage in English (default) and Spanish, as per the project submission requirements.

What factors were considered?

We considered the distinct spatial resolutions, overpass times, and detection responses of five different satellite platforms (Terra, Aqua, Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21). We accounted for historical data starting from 2000 for MODIS and 2012 for VIIRS, structuring it into 13,405 10x10 km grid cells across Peru. Statistical factors like shared activity and relative platform responses were balanced using conditional maximum likelihood.

What is the intended impact?

The tool aims to equip fire managers, emergency prevention and responders; and scientists with a reliable baseline of historical fire patterns. This enables better early warning systems, helps identify unusual burning conditions, and optimizes resource allocation during critical fire periods to protect ecosystems and communities.

What is the added value of the project?

Instead of merely overlaying incompatible data, FuegoTrazo uses an empirical calibration model to calculate a 'comparable count' of fire detections. It also introduces an experimental machine learning forecast module (HistGradientBoostingClassifier) to predict fire risks based on historical and geographical data, providing actionable predictive insights rather than just raw historical data.

What tools were used in the project?

  • Python and Jupyter for data preparation, analysis and reproductible notebooks.
  • Pandas, NumPy and SciPy for processing satellite observations and statistical analysis.
  • Scikit-learn and LightGBM for experimental forecasting and model evaluation.
  • Shapely, PyProj, R-tress and KD-trees for geographic processing and spatial queries.
  • FastAPI, Pydantic and SQLite for the historical-data and forecast API.
  • React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts and Leaflet for the web interface, charts and maps.
  • Docker, Railway, Netlify and GitHub for packaging, deployment and version control.
